The appendix support instead concerns the averaged velocity of the Föllmer flow (thm:dimfree_lip_velocity, lem:avg_velocity_lipschitz), a velocity field associated with a different transport between $\rho$ and $\pi$; no identification between the Föllmer averaged velocity and the Mean-Flow averaged velocity is established anywhere (for non-Gaussian posteriors, the case of interest, they are different fields). Moreover, the cited theorem states the Föllmer velocity transports $\rho$ to $\pi$ forward in time; under that convention the $\rho\to\pi$ one-step map adds the trajectory displacement evaluated along the forward flow, whereas the corollary and the sampler subtract an endpoint-evaluated average, so as written the construction does not even deliver a reference-to-posterior map without repairing the direction convention. and cannot be realized as a continuous or Lipschitz map $\mathcal{H}\to\mathcal{H}$

issues.failure_explanation: What is established: white noise is a.s. not $\mathcal{H}$-valued and is mutually singular with trace-class Gaussians and $\mathcal{H}$-supported posteriors on $\mathcal{H}^{-s}$ (proposition, correct). What the prose claims: that this 'rules out any regular deterministic one-step transport realized as a map $\mathcal{H}\to\mathcal{H}$', that white references are 'obstructed'/'intrinsically ill-posed due to measure singularity', and that trace-class references are necessary 'to ensure the well-posedness'. The ruling-out holds only trivially: since $\rho_{\mathrm{W}}(\mathcal{H})=0$, no map with domain $\mathcal{H}$ — regular or not — can push $\rho_{\mathrm{W}}$ forward; regularity is not the obstruction. Meanwhile the paper's own Example constructs a bounded linear (hence continuous and Lipschitz) one-step transport $\mathcal{T}=C^{1/2}$ with $\mathcal{T}_\#\rho_{\mathrm{W}}=\rho_{\mathrm{A}}$ on $\mathcal{H}^{-s}$, so regular deterministic one-step transports from the white reference do exist on the space where white noise lives; the example's closing claim that the pushforward 'cannot be realized as a continuous or Lipschitz map $\mathcal{H}\to\mathcal{H}$' is likewise misleading, since $C^{1/2}$ is bounded on $\mathcal{H}$ — only the domain's zero $\rho_{\mathrm{W}}$-measure fails. The formal content is a latent-geometry/domain mismatch, not an obstruction to regular one-step sampling.

failure_location.quote: and rules out any regular deterministic one-step transport realized as a map $\mathcal{H}\to\mathcal{H}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the obstruction claims to the established content: white-noise latents lie a.s. outside $\mathcal{H}$, so any sampler must act on distribution-valued states and the transport cannot be realized on $\mathcal{H}$ regardless of regularity; regular one-step transports from white noise exist on $\mathcal{H}^{-s}$ (the paper's own example) but are necessarily smoothing/non-invertible; the observed instability is an empirical finding.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract ('incompatible with the function-space limit'), the contribution bullet ('necessity of a prior-aligned trace-class base measure to ensure the well-posedness... while white noise is not'), the subsection framing ('White reference is obstructed in the function-space regime'), and the conclusion ('intrinsically ill-posed... due to measure singularity') claim more than Proposition prop:white_colored_singular and Example ex:direct_singular_map support; the theoretical 'necessity' argument for trace-class references is weaker than advertised (the empirical instability evidence is unaffected).
issues.title: White-noise 'obstruction' prose overstates the singularity result: the paper's own example is a Lipschitz one-step transport from the white reference
issues.why_classification: The formal results (proposition and example) are correct and survive unchanged; the repair is a local rewording of prose characterizations that preserves the design guidance and all empirical claims.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \mathrm{Lip}\big(w(\cdot;r,t)\big) \le \frac{1}{t-r}\int_r^t \mathrm{Lip}\big(v(\tau,\cdot)\big)\,d\tau \le L_0\,\frac{t+r}{2}
\frac{1}{t-r}\int_r^t v(z_\tau,\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau
\mathrm{Lip}\big(v(t,\cdot)\big)\le L_0\,t,\quad \forall\,t\in[0,1],

issues.failure_explanation: No proof is given for the lemma. Its central inequality $\mathrm{Lip}(w(\cdot;r,t))\le\frac{1}{t-r}\int_r^t\mathrm{Lip}(v(\tau,\cdot))\,d\tau$ would hold for a frozen-point time average, but the paper's averaged velocity (eq:avg_velocity_def) integrates $v$ along trajectories; its Lipschitz constant in the evaluation state involves the Jacobian of the backward flow, which by Grönwall can grow like $\exp(\int\mathrm{Lip}(v))$ and is not bounded by the average of $\mathrm{Lip}(v)$. Concretely, in one dimension $v(z,\tau)=-\lambda\tau z$ satisfies the hypothesis pattern $\mathrm{Lip}(v(\tau,\cdot))=\lambda\tau\le L_0\tau$ (with $L_0=\lambda$), yet its trajectory-averaged velocity on $[0,1]$ has $\mathrm{Lip}(w(\cdot;0,1))=e^{\lambda/2}-1>\lambda/2$, contradicting the asserted bound. (If $w$ were instead read as the frozen-point average, the inequality becomes trivial but $w$ is no longer the Mean-Flow averaged velocity, and $\mathcal{T}(\xi)=\xi-w(\xi;0,1)$ would no longer transport $\rho$ to $\pi$.) The lemma also never specifies along which flow or coupling the average is taken. The specific constants $L_0(t+r)/2$ and $L_0/2$ — hence $\mathrm{Lip}(\mathcal{T})\le 1+L_0/2$ in the corollary and main theorem — are not established.

issues.why_classification: The asserted bound is not derivable as claimed and no proof is given, so a contained but genuinely new argument is required; the natural repair materially worsens the stated constants (exponential rather than linear in $L_0$) while preserving the qualitative dimension-free Lipschitz conclusion — a limited weakening leaving a recognizable result.
